summary: Describes an efficient way to export bidirectional flows with IPFIX, representing each two-way flow as a single record. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: A conversation goes both ways. Instead of writing two notes, one for each direction, this lets the router write one note for the whole conversation.

questions: what is a biflow in ipfix
how does ipfix export bidirectional flows
what is the ipfix reverse private enterprise number
subtitle: How IPFIX can describe both directions of a conversation in a single flow record.

tldr.problem: Many flow analyses need the two directions of a conversation matched up, but exporting each direction as a separate record duplicates the flow key and pushes the matching work onto the Collector.
tldr.mechanism: A Biflow is exported as one Flow Record that holds the flow key once, plus forward values and Reverse Information Elements. Reverse elements are marked by the Private Enterprise Number 29305, and a new biflowDirection element says how source and destination were chosen.
tldr.outcome: IPFIX needs only information model extensions to carry Biflows. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated.

today: RFC 5103 is a Proposed Standard, published in January 2008. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Export Two-Way Flows Together
sections.content:
Many flow analysis tasks benefit from linking the upstream and downstream halves of a conversation. The RFC gives examples such as separating answered and unanswered TCP requests and calculating round trip times. A Biflow is a flow made of packets sent in both directions between two endpoints.

A metering process placed at a single point where traffic in both directions passes is well placed to see Biflows. In such setups the total resource needs are often lower if Biflows are assembled at the measurement interface instead of at the Collector.

The IPFIX protocol already works for this. It only needs extensions to the information model, and this document defines them: extra Information Elements for the reverse direction of each Biflow and one more element describing how direction was assigned.
sections.eli5: When two kids talk, you could keep one notebook for what each says. It is neater to keep one page for the whole chat, with a column for each kid.

sections.title: Key Terms: Uniflow, Biflow, Forward and Reverse
sections.content:
A Uniflow is a flow made only of packets from one endpoint to another. A Biflow is composed of two Uniflows so that each Non-directional Key Field is identical in both, and each Directional Key Field in one equals its reverse counterpart in the other. For example, sourceIPv4Address is a Directional Key Field and protocolIdentifier is a Non-directional one.

The Biflow Source is the endpoint named by the source Directional Key Fields, and the Biflow Destination is the endpoint named by the destination ones. The forward direction is the packets sent by the Biflow Source, described with normal Information Elements. The reverse direction is the packets sent by the Biflow Destination, described with Reverse Information Elements.

A Uniflow can be seen as a Biflow that has only a forward direction.
sections.eli5: One side of the chat is called forward and the other side is called reverse. The two sides are matched up because they share the same pair of speakers.

sections.title: Rationale and Rejected Alternatives
sections.content:
The authors considered other ways to export Biflows before choosing a single Flow Record per Biflow. The RFC lists three.

  • Export two Uniflows next to each other in the record stream. This is only an informal arrangement a Collector cannot rely on, and it duplicates the Flow Key data in each record.
  • Use the method in a draft on reducing redundancy in IPFIX and PSAMP reports, which exports the Flow Key as Common Properties and each direction as Specific Properties. That adds the overhead of a commonPropertiesId and more state to manage at both Exporter and Collector.
  • Use the protocol's Multiple Information Element feature, where the first instance of a counter is forward and the second is reverse. This conflicted with the existing counter semantics and was abandoned.
sections.eli5: The authors tried other ways to keep the two halves together, but each was either wasteful, hard to keep track of, or confusing. They picked the simplest one.

sections.title: Biflow Semantics
sections.content:
The RFC gives two reasons to treat a Biflow as one thing. Most application protocols are two-way, so a Biflow model describes network behavior more accurately. It can also improve export efficiency by removing duplicated Flow Key data, and ease the Collector's job by removing Biflow matching where possible.

A Biflow record holds each Flow Key field once, then forward and Reverse Information Elements for each non-key field. A Collector may treat a Flow Record as a Biflow record if it contains at least one Reverse Information Element and at least one Directional Key Field. A record with Reverse Information Elements but no Directional Key Fields is illegal: the Exporting Process MUST NOT send it, and the Collector SHOULD drop it and log it.

When exporting Uniflows, Exporters SHOULD use a Template with no Reverse Information Elements. A Template whose only reverse elements are counters may still be used, because a zero counter means no reverse traffic. That does not work for elements where zero has its own meaning, such as tcpControlBits.

Two further rules matter. A Biflow may only be built from packets seen in the same Observation Domain. And where a middlebox changes packets, it must be clear whether packets were metered before or after the change; the Observation Process SHOULD sit on one side of the middlebox, and the Exporter SHOULD send both the incoming value and the changed one, using the post elements of the information model.
sections.eli5: A Biflow record writes down who is talking once, then keeps two sets of counts: one for each side. If a note has reverse counts but no names, it is thrown out.

sections.title: Assigning Direction
sections.content:
Deciding which end is the "source" depends on where the Metering Process sits and what the measurement is for, so the RFC describes three methods. Because the choice follows from the position of the Metering Process, it can be configured at the Exporter or Collector out of band.

  • By initiator (5.1): the Metering Process SHOULD make the flow initiator the Biflow Source where possible. A rough approximation is to assume the first packet seen starts the Biflow, which can be improved with protocol knowledge such as TCP flags. A long flow that is split by an active timeout can spoil this assumption.
  • By perimeter (5.2): if there is a stable set of addresses inside a perimeter and no need to know the initiator, the Biflow Source SHOULD be the endpoint outside the perimeter. The interior address set is not exported.
  • Arbitrary (5.3): in a network core with no stable perimeter and no way to find the initiator, the Metering Process MAY assign direction arbitrarily. It SHOULD be consistent and keep the direction for the lifetime of the Biflow, even across an active timeout.
sections.eli5: Someone has to be called the first speaker. You can pick whoever spoke first, whoever is outside the house, or just pick one and stick with it.

sections.title: Record Representation: Reverse Information Elements
sections.content:
Reverse Information Elements are a separate dimension of the Information Element space. The RFC assigns Private Enterprise Number (PEN) 29305, the Reverse PEN, to signify an IPFIX Reverse Information Element. To make the reverse twin of a forward element in a Template, set the enterprise bit and give the same element number under the Reverse PEN. This means new elements added to the IANA space need no matching reverse entry.

Some elements cannot be reversed because they describe the record as a whole or are used by the protocol itself. They are flowId, templateId, observationDomainId and commonPropertiesId, the process configuration and process statistics elements, paddingOctets, and biflowDirection. An Exporter MUST NOT export a Template with a reverse counterpart of such an element, and a Collector MAY discard it. Elements commonly used as keys, such as header fields, are reversible.

The Reverse PEN covers only IANA-registered elements. A private enterprise that wants reversible elements of its own MAY reserve one bit of the Information Element ID; for instance, reserving the most significant of the fifteen available bits would make IDs 0x4000 to 0x7FFF the reverse of 0x0000 to 0x3FFF.

Appendix A walks through a Template of 11 fields (Template Set length 64) that pairs flowStartSeconds, octetTotalCount and packetTotalCount with their reverse versions, plus a data set for a typical HTTP transaction.
sections.eli5: Every normal label gets a twin stamped with a special mark, meaning the same thing but for the other side. A few labels, like the page number, have no twin.

sections.title: The biflowDirection Element and IANA Actions
sections.content:
biflowDirection records which method assigned Biflow Source and Destination. It is an unsigned8 identifier, Information Element number 239. It may appear in a Flow Record, or be applied to a whole Exporting Process or Observation Domain with IPFIX Options. If it is absent, direction assignment is assumed to be configured out of band. When sent through Options it SHOULD be sent reliably; over unreliable transport such as UDP it SHOULD appear in each Flow Record.

The IANA Considerations section records two actions. IANA assigned Private Enterprise Number 29305 as the "IPFIX Reverse Information Element Private Enterprise", with the authors as contact, and assigned element number 239 for biflowDirection. Its values are static and need no IANA sub-registry.
sections.eli5: A small label can say how the first speaker was chosen, so anyone reading the notes knows the rule that was used.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The security section is a single sentence: the same security considerations as for the IPFIX Protocol apply. The RFC defines no extra security mechanism for Biflow export.
sections.eli5: Nothing new is added here. The same safety rules as the main IPFIX rulebook apply.

items.label: initiator
items.desc: The Biflow Source is the flow initiator, by best-effort detection.

items.label: reverseInitiator
items.desc: The Biflow Destination is the flow initiator; lets an Exporter revise its estimate without re-encoding.

items.label: perimeter
items.desc: The Biflow Source is the endpoint outside a defined perimeter.
